newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Heidemij to focus on internal growth.
newsitem.headline: Heidemij to focus on internal growth.

text.p: Engineering consultancy Heidemij said on Tuesday it would slow the pace of acquisitions after a bumper year of takeovers in 1996.
"We are now more oriented towards getting more out of the company than continuing to acquire at the same rate," chairman Frans Luttmer told a news conference.
He said the company would continue its gradual expansion into Latin America and South East Asia, but added any acquisitions would be small scale initially.
"In Asia steps will be cautious, (acquisitions) will not be more than some two million guilders at a time," Luttmer said.
He said improved synergies within the group would gradually boost profit margins, pressured by Heidemij's policy to hive off non-consolidated shareholdings and invest in core business.
"Inevitably (this policy) means that top-line turnover grows faster than the bottom line, so profit margins fall," he said.

In addition, substantial goodwill payments for acquisitions pressured solvency ratios (group equity as a percentage of the balance sheet total), which fell to 33.5 percent in 1996 from a year-earlier 42.6 percent.
The acquisition of Piedmont Olsen Hensley, in U.S. South Carolina, accounted for the lion's share, Luttmer added.

Other acquisitions last year included Epteos of Spain and a 35 percent stake in Sageos of France. In the Netherlands, Heidemij acquired the remaining 30 percent of shares it did not already own in Grabowsky&Poort, which in turn took over project and building management agency Starke Diekstra.
The firm also opened new offices in Pakistan and Kazakhstan.
Heidemij said earlier on Tuesday it had acquired Chilean engineering consultancy Geotecnica Consultores for an undisclosed sum.
Heidemij earlier reported 1996 net profit from ordinary operations rose four percent to 28.1 million guilders.
However, a two million guilder one-off charge resulting from the failed merger with sector peer DHV cut its net profit to 26.1 million guilders.
